newsitem.title: ROMANIA: ROMANIAN ELECTIONS TOP GOVERNMENT'S AGENDA.
newsitem.headline: ROMANIAN ELECTIONS TOP GOVERNMENT'S AGENDA.

text.p: The Romanian government decided on Wednesday voters' cards for Romanian electors in the November polls were not absolutely necessary and identity cards were equally valid.
"This decision does not absolve local administration of its duty to distribute voters' cards," government spokesman Ioan Rosca said at a briefing after the cabinet's weekly meeting.

He said printing and distribution of voters' cards, essential for some 17 million Romanians eligible to vote in November parliamentary and presidential polls, was behind schedule. Not all voters will be able to receive their cards in time, he said.
Other issues on Wednesday's agenda included:
* decision revising the 1996 social insurance budget. Revenues rose by 588.7 billion lei to 6.2 trillion lei and spending grew by 739.6 billion lei to 6.2 trillion lei.
* decision to pay farmers 7.0 billion lei to cover losses caused by natural disasters in the second half of 1996.
* Agriculture Minister Alexandru Lapusan's report on autumn farming works. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
